title: Aggregate commands
description: How every aggregate's commands are reached and answer, whichever interface runs them: each interface names one specific command, a refusal gives every reason and changes nothing, fields come as JSON, the CLI answers within its budget from a cached schema, and the plugin's skills write only through the commands' tools. How each interface names a command and shows a refusal is its own pattern's. Its code is written one way: a command's identity, an aggregate's repository and its pattern commands' handlers are generated from the records, a Remove takes its record whole, a command file restates nothing of its definition, built-in modules are named with node:, and an outside program runs from an argument array.
notes: Each use case that writes an aggregate follows it; the aggregate's own rules are its use case's requirements and its invariants.

title: Aggregate queries
description: How every query is reached and answers, whichever interface asks it: each interface names one specific query, a query answers from its read model alone and changes nothing, one that finds nothing says what it could not find, and each read model follows the records it reads. How each interface names a query and shows its answer or refusal is its own pattern's.
notes: Each domain with read models follows it; what a query answers is its use case's requirements, and what a read model holds is the read model's own fields.

title: Aggregate tests
description: How an aggregate's tests are written: each sits under the one record it proves, as that record's test kind, runs at the lowest level that can observe its result and that its kind allows, and starts from its aggregate's own data set; each of a domain's checks has a test in the domain's folder that breaks it.

title: App code
description: How the web app's code is written, so that every page and every agent's change reads the same way and stays easy to change: where layout and style live, colors as tokens, generic components, labels, accessible names, spelling and addresses. The app lives in `app/src`; Platform (`LA-PLT`) follows this pattern for all of it, and holds the tests that prove it for the whole app. How the app behaves for the person using it (hover, the stage and its floating panels, the page bar, motion, row links, addresses, touch and stability) is the App experience pattern, `LA-PAT-APP-UX`.
notes:
The rules come from problems the app has had: a button laid over a heading with CSS that overlapped the list below it, a page style that reached every `header` element, a hand-made plural that read wrong, and spelling that drifted between British and American.

## How a domain uses the pattern

The domain links the pattern with `follows`. The pattern has no settings: every rule applies to all of the domain's code. Each rule is proved by a test in `app/test` (most in `standards.test.tsx`) that reads the source or renders the main pages, and that names the file and line to fix when it fails. R21's tests also run knip on the app, the engine and the desktop app. Code that carries out one of its rules meets it. The engine's code follows the Aggregate commands and Aggregate tests patterns, `LA-PAT-AGGREGATE-COMMANDS` and `LA-PAT-AGGREGATE-TESTS`.

## Rules

- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R01`: layout lives in the markup.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R02`: styles are set by class.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R03`: colors and shadows are tokens.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R04`: generic components know nothing of specs.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R05`: kind labels become plural only through `plural()`, and lowercase only through `lowerLabel()`.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R06`: every control has an accessible name.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R07`: American spelling.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R10`: every grid says its columns.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R15`: themes only set tokens.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R19`: one address per thing, made by `addressOf`.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R20`: changes are hard cutovers, with no compatibility layer.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R21`: nothing outlives its purpose: no unused code, style, command or icon, and every mark the Graph and ERD stages draw is in their key.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R25`: a store's snapshot is stable.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R26`: browser tests fail on page errors and share one desktop stand-in.
- `LA-PAT-APP-CODE-R27`: record IDs are ordered by the one ID collator of each package.

The numbers of the rules that moved to App experience (R08, R09, R11 to R14, R16 and R17) are not reused; new rules here continue from R28.

title: App experience
description: How the web app behaves for the person using it, so that every page feels the same to the hand and the eye: what shows a hover, how the stage sits behind floating panels that resize, what the page bar and a stage's own tools hold, how a breadcrumb collapses, how things move, how a row leads to its record and a card takes its one action, how every open thing keeps an address, how tools open over the stage rather than replace it, how it all works by touch, that nothing jumps, that actions look like actions, and that it stays within its performance budgets. The app lives in `app/src`; Platform (`LA-PLT`) follows this pattern for all of it, and holds the tests that prove it for the whole app. How the code itself is written (layout in markup, classes, tokens, generic components, labels, names and spelling) is the App code pattern, `LA-PAT-APP-CODE`.
notes:
## How a domain uses the pattern

The domain links the pattern with `follows`. The pattern has no settings: every rule applies to all of the domain's pages. Each rule is proved by a test in `app/test` that reads the source or renders the main pages, and that names the file and line to fix when it fails. `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R08` is proved in a real browser by the stability suite (`app/stability`, `npm --prefix app run test:stability`), and at the source by `app/test/nothing-jumps.test.tsx`. `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11` is proved on the production build by the performance suite (`app/perf`, `npm --prefix app run test:perf`). `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R10` is proved in a real browser by the accessibility suite (`app/a11y`, `npm --prefix app run test:a11y`). `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12` is proved by a sweep over the repo's own specs in the unit run and in a real browser by the stability suite.

## Rules

- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R01`: everything clickable shows a hover state.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R02`: the stage behind, panels floating over it, every panel edge resizes.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R03`: the page bar holds the page's controls; a stage's own tools float in the open space.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R04`: motion is shared and optional.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R05`: a row that leads to one record is one link.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R06`: every open thing has an address.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R07`: everything works by touch.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R08`: nothing jumps.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R09`: actions look like actions.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R10`: every page passes the accessibility audit.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R11`: Lathe stays within its performance budgets.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R12`: every drawn box shows its name.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R13`: labels read in sentence case.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R14`: a card has one primary action, taken by clicking anywhere on it.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R15`: a stage with one folder shows its records directly.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R16`: one breadcrumb, collapsed past three places.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R17`: every stage works on every focus.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R20`: nothing replaces the stage: tools open as panels over it.
- `LA-PAT-APP-UX-R24`: node text has three levels from one scale.

New rules continue from UX-R25.

title: CLI steps
description: How the command line carries out a flow's step: by the one command named for the step's command or query, and how it shows a refusal. Each use case's flow is written once; the CLI's version of it is derived from this.

title: Field inputs
description: The shared inputs every aggregate's editor builds its fields from, one per column type, so that each editor is written for its aggregate while a text, number, choice or link field looks and behaves the same everywhere.

title: HTTP API steps
description: How the local server's API carries out a flow's step for the product's own app: by the one route of the step's command or query, and how it answers a refusal. Each use case's flow is written once; the API's version of it is derived from this.

title: MCP tool steps
description: How the plugin's MCP tools carry out a flow's step for an Agent: by the one tool named for the step's command or query, and how they return a refusal. Each use case's flow is written once; the tools' version of it is derived from this.

title: Package API steps
description: How the package's exports carry out a flow's step in an Agent's script: by the exported function for it, and how a refusal reaches the script. Each use case's flow is written once; the package's version of it is derived from this.

title: Page steps
description: How the web app and the desktop app carry out a flow's step: in a view that presents the step's command or query, by the person the interface lists for its use case, and how they show a refusal. Each use case's flow is written once; their version of it is derived from this.

title: Record data file
description: How an author reaches the data file that holds the record in front, without leaving the desktop app: reveal it, open it in an editor, or copy its ID.

title: Record page
description: What every aggregate's page shares, whatever it shows: one address per record, its title and kind, its links in and out, and the way it opens in a tab, the wiki card and the stage. What a page shows of its own aggregate is that page's view requirements.

title: Shell actions
description: How the desktop shell takes an action a page asks for: by a known action and an ID only, never a path, so that a page cannot make the shell open, reveal or run anything it names.
